lessons.title: Symmetry is useful until it hides the domain
lessons.lesson: Code is not good only because it looks balanced. Symmetry is useful until it hides an asymmetric domain rule. When one branch contains a real special case or business rule, that branch is load-bearing. Do not replace it with tidy map dispatch or matching branches only for visual balance. Symmetric code can look complete and stop necessary review.
lessons.trigger_context: Refactoring asymmetric branches, special cases, dispatch maps, or code whose visual balance can hide domain behavior.
lessons.proof_pattern: Compare the explicit special-case branch with the proposed abstraction. Confirm that the business rule remains correct and directly findable. If one tidy branch performs domain work and another exists only to complete a visual pattern, the symmetry is false.

lessons.title: Comments explain intent, danger, or constraints
lessons.lesson: Use comments for intent, danger, required procedure, constraints, surprises, or an incident that a future reader cannot reconstruct from code or history. Do not use comments to narrate visible code. Names and structure must explain what the code does. If the action is unclear, rewrite the code instead of adding a narration comment. Preserve the reason and each load-bearing assumption.
lessons.trigger_context: Writing or reviewing comments, unclear names, legacy constraints, dangerous assumptions, or incident-shaped behavior.
lessons.proof_pattern: Delete comments that restate the next line. Keep a comment such as: `Reverse order is required because the legacy importer expects newest-first.` If removal loses only narration, delete the comment. If removal loses a constraint that cannot be recovered from the code, keep it.

lessons.title: Expose cost and state; hide noise
lessons.lesson: Make state and cost visible at the seam where a caller would otherwise have to guess. I/O, allocation, locking, blocking, side effects, cache mutation, and other important state changes must be visible in the call contract. Hide boilerplate, plumbing, and framework ceremony. An immutable-looking API that secretly mutates a cache forces every caller to inspect its implementation.
lessons.trigger_context: Designing APIs around I/O, caches, locks, allocation, mutation, blocking calls, or framework plumbing.
lessons.proof_pattern: A function named `load_config()` that silently performs network I/O or mutates a cache hides cost. A function named `fetch_config()` that hides import ceremony hides noise. Inspect signatures, names, and call sites. Callers must be able to identify expensive or stateful behavior without opening the implementation.

lessons.title: Delete the clever line when the plain line reads better
lessons.lesson: Cleverness costs each future reader. Plainness costs the writer once. If a first-time reader must reread an expression and gains no necessary insight, the compression failed. Prefer a plain structure that exposes each mental operation over a dense expression whose main benefit is brevity.
lessons.trigger_context: Dense expressions, nested ternaries, stacked comprehensions, clever one-line statements, or code that requires rereading without adding insight.
lessons.proof_pattern: Replace a nested ternary, or a comprehension that combines generation, filtering, tuple unpacking, and transformation, with a plain `if`/`elif`/`else` block or short loop. Confirm that each decision is visible and behavior is unchanged.

lessons.title: Flatten control flow before it becomes a pyramid
lessons.lesson: Keep nesting to about three levels. Prevent pyramids while writing the code. Guard clauses state what is true at each point and let the reader continue. Use early returns for guards, invert conditions to fail fast, extract inner work into named functions, and replace conditional pyramids with early-exit chains. Use indentation for real nesting, not for chained validation. Each level adds cognitive cost.
lessons.trigger_context: Nested validation, deep dispatch loops, chained guards, `try` and `if` pyramids, or control flow approaching three indentation levels.
lessons.proof_pattern: Convert three levels of nested validation into guard clauses. Convert a `try`/`for`/`try`/`if`/`if` dispatch pyramid into named handlers called by a flat coordinator. Verify that each extracted branch has one clear contract and that behavior is unchanged.

lessons.title: Merge by intent before side
lessons.lesson: In multi-contributor code, neither ours versus theirs nor newest versus oldest is the rule. A conflict-free merge proves textual compatibility only. It does not prove semantic safety. State each side's intent. Preserve compatible work. Keep older invariant-bearing behavior unless the current task explicitly replaces it. Supersede work only when one intent truly replaces the other, integrates it more safely, or the responsible maintainer approves the change. For hotspot files, compare changed regions with recent commits even when Git reports no conflict. Escalate large or behavior-shaping overlap before product or user-interface behavior is lost.
lessons.trigger_context: Merge conflicts, conflict-free same-file overlap, contributor synchronization, hotspot files, branch promotion, or deployment checkpoint preparation.
lessons.proof_pattern: Identify hotspot files and invariants that must survive. Compare contributor references and recent changes. Integrate compatible intentions. Pause before critical uploads or promotions. A clean merge is not proof until preserved behavior is checked.

lessons.title: Use negative space as punctuation
lessons.lesson: Blank lines separate completed thoughts. Add a rest after a resolved guard, before a terminal return, between distinct concerns, after a loop before its conclusion, and between functions when one thought ends and another starts. Apply this rule at line and function scale. Do not add spacing by quota. Code without rests is difficult to scan. Blank lines every few lines create false boundaries. Let meaning determine spacing.
lessons.trigger_context: Blank lines, vertical spacing, cramped functions, terminal returns, guards, loops, formatting, or code rhythm.
lessons.proof_pattern: Read the function as paragraphs. Each blank line must identify a completed thought or transition. Add a rest where a guard, concern, loop-to-conclusion transition, terminal return, or function boundary needs one. Remove automatic spacing that has no semantic boundary.

lessons.title: Resolve reusable article media from canonical references
lessons.lesson: For reusable article media, store a stable media reference. At render time, resolve the current poster, title, caption, credit, and other display metadata from the canonical library record. Do not freeze this metadata in article HTML as a second source of truth. Through sanitization, explicitly allow only the stable reference and required behavior attributes, such as `data-video-*` identifiers or fullscreen flags. The editor preview and public renderer must resolve the same canonical record.
lessons.trigger_context: Reusable gallery or video blocks, WYSIWYG sanitization, article payloads, CMS media libraries, editor previews, or React and Astro rendering.
lessons.proof_pattern: Inspect stored HTML. It must contain the stable reference and behavior attributes, but no frozen canonical display metadata. Verify that sanitization preserves the allowed attributes. Verify that resolver output controls the poster, caption, credit, and fullscreen behavior. React and Astro renderers must use the same current library record.

lessons.title: Checkpoint broad investigations, then rewind to findings
lessons.lesson: Before a broad investigation that will create substantial scratch context, create a top-level checkpoint with a precise goal. Explore, then rewind immediately with a concise factual report. Include findings, decisions, unresolved risks, and exact next actions. A checkpoint is not a save command for ordinary edits. It is a context-cost boundary for exploration. It is incomplete until the rewind report replaces the scratch trail.
lessons.trigger_context: Before broad repository archaeology, unfamiliar subsystem mapping, dependency investigation, or exploratory work that requires many reads and searches but whose raw trail will not matter after the conclusion.
lessons.proof_pattern: Start with `checkpoint(goal)`. Perform exploratory reads and searches inside it. Run `rewind(report)` before yielding. After rewind, active context must contain the compact report instead of raw exploration logs.

lessons.title: Search limits bound absence claims
lessons.lesson: Interpret each search result according to its reported coverage. A timeout, result cap, skipped path, oversized-resource note, partial byte scan, or virtual-resource fallback means that the search did not prove absence. Narrow the scope, page the results, search the source path directly, or change strategy before you conclude that a symbol, file, or pattern is absent. Never convert partial execution into a definitive negative claim.
lessons.trigger_context: When grep, glob, read, archive search, internal-resource search, or a repository-wide lookup returns no matches, reaches a limit, times out, or reports partial coverage.
lessons.proof_pattern: Support an absence claim with a search that reports complete coverage, or label the claim as partial. A timeout, cap, skipped path, or oversized-resource notice requires a narrower follow-up search rather than a negative conclusion.

lessons.title: Use selectors to recover only hidden evidence
lessons.lesson: Structural reads, converted documents, archives, databases, internal URLs, and large artifacts are designed for paging. When a read operation summarizes code or reports elided ranges, use the exact recovery selector that it emits. Do not reread the full file or guess hidden bodies. Use `:raw` only when verbatim bytes or source text are required. Page `artifact://` and `history://` resources by range. Percent-encode literal colon, question-mark, or hash characters in path-like internal URLs. Narrow recovery preserves evidence and limits context growth.
lessons.trigger_context: When a read operation returns a structural summary, elision footer, oversized-artifact notice, converted document, archive member, database view, internal URL, or path that contains selector punctuation.
lessons.proof_pattern: Follow a summarized or oversized read with the exact named range or raw selector. Add only the required hidden section to context. Do not base an edit or claim on elided content. Correct malformed selector-like paths instead of silently widening the read.

lessons.title: Choose context actions by the source of weight
lessons.lesson: Do not wait until context pressure causes failure. Do not apply one cleanup action blindly. Select the action from the context composition. Compact reasoning or history when conversation is heavy. Shake or elide bulky tool results and images when evidence dominates. Start fresh only to reset provider state while preserving the transcript. Hand off when remaining context is too large or the work needs a clean continuation. For long autonomous objectives, use goal mode. Treat budget exhaustion as a pause or continuation state, never as proof of completion.
lessons.trigger_context: When context usage grows, tool or image output dominates, provider state is inconsistent, a long task needs continuation, or an autonomous objective approaches its token or time budget.
lessons.proof_pattern: State the dominant source of context weight before selecting an action. Verify the result through changed context composition or a clean continuation. Report goal completion only with explicit evidence. If the budget ends, preserve the objective and current status.

lessons.title: Prefer the workstation's proven topology
lessons.lesson: When you adapt a project to a workstation, start from the last proven service split and use the path of least resistance. Do not turn a startup repair into a topology migration only because another arrangement looks cleaner. If the known-good Windows and WSL topology runs databases and infrastructure in WSL while code, Node.js runtimes, editors, and dependency trees remain on Windows, restore that split unless evidence requires a move. First reproduce the known-good launch. Preserve OS-native dependencies. Make only the smallest changes needed for ports, readiness, and lifecycle. Harden each cross-OS seam at its boundary. Do not use the seam as a reason to relocate the full application. Recover and verify the last working path before you install runtimes or rebuild dependencies in another operating system.
lessons.trigger_context: Starting or adapting an existing project on a Windows and WSL workstation, especially when the service worked recently and native dependencies differ between operating systems.
lessons.proof_pattern: Identify the last proven topology. Classify each service by its current host operating system. Restore that topology without migration. Verify the user-visible path. Then make one bounded environment change at a time.
